## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 46 (Vin IV 302), titled *Bhojanadāna* ("Giving food to a non-monastic"), governs the distribution of almsfood by Buddhist nuns [SuttaCentral; Bechert et al. 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun commits an expiation (*pācittiya*) offence if she gives soft or solid food with her own hands to a householder (*agārika*), a male wanderer (*paribbājaka*), or a female wanderer (*paribbājikā*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the word-commentary, *agārika* is defined as anyone residing in a household, while *paribbājaka* and *paribbājikā* comprise wanderers of other sects, explicitly excluding Buddhist monastics—namely monks (*bhikkhu*), nuns (*bhikkhunī*), probationers (*sikkhamānā*), and male and female novices (*sāmaṇera*, *sāmaṇerī*) [Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997]. The rule corresponds functionally to the monks' Pācittiya 41, though the monks' rule mentions naked ascetics (*acelaka*) whereas the nuns' rule designates householders [Wijayaratna 1990; Hüsken 1997]. According to the exemption clauses, no offence is incurred if the monastic has another person hand over the food or simply leaves it for an ascetic to take [Wijayaratna 1990].

Direct parallels to the rule are attested across the Vinayas of several early Buddhist schools, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 112), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 130), Mahāsaṅghika (Bi Vb Pc 81), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga (Pc 81) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread internal reuse across the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga—sharing lengthy boilerplate passages particularly with Pācittiya 28 (§0.4–2.1.10), Pācittiya 48, and Pācittiya 81—alongside automatic cross-language alignments with Tibetan canonical Vinaya texts, including the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) [DharmaNexus].
